gaps
gaps · 3 records
  1. Not a complete historical record of all statements or every intraperiod update. No claim that no other revisions existed.
  2. Published revenue precision ranges from $0.1m releases to $0.001m filing detail; no material range outcome depends on precision.
  3. Quarterly outlook net-income/EPS use company-specific non-GAAP tax and exclusions; they are not GAAP EBIT margin targets.
methodology

error
(actual / original range midpoint - 1) × 100; positive = actual above midpoint
range

interpretation
Beat frequency can reflect conservatism, demand surprises or guidance policy. It is not a CEO ranking or a multiplier applied to valuation.
unmatured
Pending is never zero or miss.

model Definition
model Definition · 5 fields
margin
EBIT after ongoing SBC, depreciation and R&D, before interest; no automatic non-GAAP EBITDA substitution
sales To Capital
Incremental revenue / net operating reinvestment, not revenue / gross capital spending
tax
Normalized cash tax rate on positive operating profit; model existing losses/NOLs separately, no cash tax benefit for losses without realizability
stable Reinvestment
g / terminal ROIC of NOPAT; terminal capital efficiency reconciled with margin/tax
sales To Capital Fade
After the explicitly specified capital-efficiency years, fade linearly to terminal ROIC / [terminal EBIT margin × (1 − normalized tax)] by the last forecast year.

wacc Status
Scenario judgment; not estimated market beta/spread. Growth-company operating and financing risk warrant explicit sensitivity, not false precision.
formula
Cost of equity = USD risk-free + assumed beta × chosen ERP; WACC also depends on debt weights/cost and normalized tax. No current beta or debt spread measured.
valuation Gates
valuation Gates · 5 records
  1. Calendar2026 starting anchors are forecasts, not actuals. Do not discount all 2026 cash flow as if still future on October 17; use valuation-date stub and actual H1.
  2. Explicit equipment/prepayment/install schedule required: H1 capital cash uses $633.5m exceed H1 revenue. Proposed sales/capital is only a diagnostic, not funded capex plan.
  3. Reconcile October cash/share/debt after completed ATM and expansion spending. June cash plus ATM proceeds is not current cash.
  4. Resolve note optionality under mutually exclusive fair-value-claim, if-converted and principal-only sensitivities.
  5. Retain Amazon warrant and employee award scenarios without double-counting contra-revenue, grant value and shares.
uncertainties
uncertainties · 4 records
  1. Ten-quarter revenue record is mostly within range, but gross margin and EPS misses show weaker profitability forecasting.
  2. Domestic production differentiation is management assertion; customers may still pressure price or shift architectures.
  3. Capacity projections assume installation, qualification, yield, key components, sales and collections all occur on time.
  4. WACC 13.5% and terminal ROIC 11% are judgments; downside includes destruction of capital even if revenue grows.
not Used
not Used · 4 records
  1. Current share price as calibration target
  2. Unverified consensus forecasts
  3. Unwatched video claims
  4. Arbitrary management credibility multipliers

stub Policy
The 2026 bridge is a June-to-December liquidity roll-forward. It is separate from 2027–2036 FCFF and is not the full future FCFF stub at October 17. For an October 17 valuation, estimate cash at that date using post-June actual/known transactions and cash use, then include only remaining October 17–December 31 FCFF. Never charge July–October cash uses twice or add June cash plus raises as current excess cash. The disclosed June balance and full H2 envelope bracket rather than verify current cash.

double Counting Rule
Amounts overlap across principal/carrying/fair value, cash/financing, RPO/customer contracts, or rent/capitalized leases. Use mutually consistent treatments.
integration Policy

summary
Provisional research assumptions only. A high-risk capacity-led turnaround in datacenter optics, with substantial funding needs before durable GAAP profitability.

rationale
rationale · 10 fields
growth
60% is year 1 growth. The staged profile then uses 40%, 30%, 20%, 15%, 10%, 8%, 5%, 3%, and 2.5% at these defaults. Quarter 3 guidance and capacity expansion support a front-loaded structure; the annual path is analyst judgment, not management guidance. Each simulated initial-growth input changes the whole same weighted path.
target Margin
12% mature GAAP EBIT margin is reached in year 6. At the reported starting loss, the staged path is −5%,0%,5%,8%,10%,12% before maturity. This is a conditional utilization and operating-leverage judgment; no non-GAAP net margin is substituted.
tax
25% applies only to positive modeled EBIT. This is a normalized mature rate; no tax refund or verified NOL benefit is assumed during losses.
sales Capital
0.8x is initial incremental sales/capital, requiring $1.25 investment per $1 extra revenue in years 1–2. It rises to 1.6x by years 6–7 as capacity is used. Years 8–10 fade capital intensity toward (1 + terminal growth) × margin × (1 − tax) / terminal ROIC, ending at 1.084x at defaults to align year 10 and terminal economics. The whole path is an explicit assumption, not a reported ratio.
terminal ROIC
10% assumes capital utilization improves in maturity but grants no excess return versus the high constant model discount rate.
wacc
13.5% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.8 plus a 1-point extra equity allowance, 10% target debt and a 3.5-point debt spread reflect concentrated customers, execution and funding risk. These are judgments, not quoted borrowing terms.
terminal Growth
2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
years
10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
other Claims
0 means no additional user-entered claim beyond the separate explicit current claims model. Do not enter the same modeled claims again. The separate source-dated current claims model deducts the disclosed convertible fair-value proxy and vendor financing once, and uses an explicit intrinsic customer-warrant scenario. Counterfactual note conversion and the incomplete known-ATM pro forma are separate sensitivities. Current employee awards and warrant time value remain incomplete.
other Assets
0 is an additional-asset assumption beyond source cash and any explicitly selected financing proceeds. It is not proof that every other nonoperating asset is absent.

model Limits
model Limits · 2 records
  1. This staged capacity assumption set produces negative operating enterprise value and five cash-burning forecast years. It is a conditional operating stress case, not a standalone fair-value estimate; financing, default, recovery and detailed maintenance replacement remain unmodeled.
  2. The simple model has no financing or default-probability schedule; a large terminal value can conceal years of cash burn.

normalization
For 2030 onward, explicitly derive capex from D&A plus growth-asset cash investment and operating WC. Fade total net investment coefficient to (1+g) / 0.9777778 = 1.048295 by 2036; this aligns the current-year revenue increment with forward-funded NOPAT*g/ROIC, matching original 11% terminal ROIC / 15% EBIT / 25% tax. D&A reaches 5% of revenue; not a company target.
conditions
conditions · 5 records
  1. Factory cash capex envelopes are analytical; no disclosed company 2027 dollar budget was found.
  2. 2027 base output needs sustained qualification, acceptable yield, customer acceptance and working-capital turns.
  3. AR concentration, supplier terms and bank acceptances can materially increase cash funding. Bank acceptances are financing if classified as debt; exclude from operating payables in that convention.
  4. Machinery useful lives span 2–20 years; new assets must start depreciating on commissioning.
  5. Retain lease rents in EBIT and use actual rental/deposit cash timing; do not deduct the operating-lease liability again under this operating-cost convention.

formulas
formulas · 5 fields
fcff
EBIT - cash tax on EBIT + D&A - gross capital cash spending - increase in other operating working capital + increase in customer advances.
capital Cash Spending
PPE/intangible cash purchases + capital supplier advances not already in those purchases + capitalized site purchases. Reclassification of existing prepayments/CIP is not a new cash use.
customer Advances
Ending = opening + new cash advances - recognized prepaid revenue - refunds (+ FX/acquisition adjustments where applicable).
funding Need
Peak cash uses + debt service + cash reserve - opening usable cash - net cash proceeds actually received - available committed credit draws. FCFF alone omits financing costs and principal maturity timing.
terminal
Terminal net reinvestment = terminal NOPAT * stable growth / terminal ROIC; customer-advance movement must be included consistently.
cautions
cautions · 4 records
  1. All future investment schedules are analytical sensitivities anchored to disclosed spending/capacity, not disclosed future budgets. Cumulative peaks are not precise financing forecasts.
  2. Economic FCFF retains SBC as compensation expense. Strict cash liquidity adds back noncash SBC and separately subtracts award withholding/buybacks; modeled 1% AAOI and 3% NBIS SBC addbacks below are illustrations, and dilution must be recognized once.
  3. NBIS 2026 guide is modeled as cash-equivalent capital spending. If guidance includes accrued equipment additions, adjust payment timing and vendor-capital payables before using the H2 bridge. $973.3m H1 additions not yet paid cannot simply be added to cash capex twice.
  4. Annual average capacity and gross deployment are distinct. Margin, replacement cost and commissioning schedules must change coherently when the physical build or economic useful life changes.
as Of Stub Policy
The 2026 bridge is a June-to-December liquidity roll-forward. It is separate from 2027–2036 FCFF and is not the full future FCFF stub at October 17. For an October 17 valuation, estimate cash at that date using post-June actual/known transactions and cash use, then include only remaining October 17–December 31 FCFF. Never charge July–October cash uses twice or add June cash plus raises as current excess cash. The disclosed June balance and full H2 envelope bracket rather than verify current cash.

bridge Methods
bridge Methods · 3 fields
default
default · 5 fields
label
Dated disclosed-market-claim bridge
formula
Common residual = DCF enterprise value + same-date unrestricted cash - bank debt - vendor financing - disclosed fair value of entire convertible instrument - other separately reviewed claims. Apply warrants separately.
denominator
Same-date common outstanding, 74.998m or 84.386m, rounded as filed. Do not add convertible shares.
not Current
June 30, 2026 note fair value is not an October 17 quote. It includes market-priced conversion optionality and depends on market stock prices, rates and credit. This conservative hybrid bridge is not a self-consistent intrinsic option valuation.
book Value Rule
Replace the book convertible amount with disclosed fair value; do not subtract both.
if Converted
if Converted · 4 fields
label
All-share settlement sensitivity; hypothetical, excludes option time value
formula
Remove the whole convertible claim, then add principalMillions * conversionRate / 1000 to common shares. No new cash is received on debt conversion.
selection Caution
Do not automatically assume holders exchange a principal claim for shares worth less than principal. A below-strike if-converted outcome is a hypothetical settlement scenario, not a rational-holder default.
intrinsic Settlement Alternative
Ignoring time value and legal timing, common price solves value available before notes = basicShares * price + max(notePrincipal, conversionShares * price). Equivalent to lower of principal-subtraction and all-share-conversion values before floor and other option claims.
principal Only
principal Only · 2 fields
label
Principal-only sensitivity; not option-inclusive valuation
note
Principal is the contractual maturity amount; carrying amount includes issuance premium and unamortized costs. Neither captures the economic value of conversion optionality. Do not present either as fair value.

current Vesting Caution

default Scenario

minimum Scenario

intrinsic Exercise Formula
If pre-warrant equity / shares exceeds strike, price = (pre-warrant equity + strike * eligibleWarrantShares) / (shares + eligibleWarrantShares); otherwise use pre-warrant equity / shares. Floor negative equity at zero for common price.
exercise Proceeds Rule
Add proceeds once only if adding gross exercise shares; alternatively solve net-share dilution without a proceeds addition.
limits
limits · 2 records
  1. Intrinsic exercise ignores remaining time value and vesting/settlement details; it is not current warrant fair value.
  2. Keep reported net-revenue and GAAP SBC baseline unchanged. Avoid adding a second blanket warrant-dollar claim on top of explicit warrant dilution. Future revenue reductions and future vesting can overlap economically; full-cap sensitivity is intentionally conservative.

rationale
rationale · 4 records
  1. Front-load growth to reflect the stated near-term ramp, then slow growth substantially rather than perpetuating 60% for years.
  2. Move margin to zero in year 2 and 12% in year 6 only as conditional operating leverage; non-GAAP net profit is not GAAP EBIT.
  3. Improve sales-to-capital from 0.8 to 1.6 as utilization improves; this is an assumption, not a measured marginal ratio.
  4. No observed share price or desired price target was used to select the path. A zero common residual remains a legitimate conditional result.

display Rules
display Rules · 5 records
  1. Show enterprise value and negative residual separately from the limited-liability common floor of $0.
  2. A zero DCF residual does not mean the traded stock or abandonment/turnaround option has literally zero value.
  3. Show peak cumulative negative FCFF and financing shortfall; no assumption that new equity can be raised without dilution.
  4. Do not add new-financing cash without adding new shares, and do not subtract financing proceeds from FCFF.
  5. A staged illustration is more informative than the old nine-negative-year smooth fade, but remains conditional rather than fully financed.

terminal Capital Intensity Formula
(1 + terminalGrowth) * targetMargin * (1 - tax) / terminalROIC
late Capital Formula
inverseSalesCapital = (1 - fadeWeight) / (2 * sampledSalesCapital) + fadeWeight * terminalCapitalIntensity; salesCapital = 1 / inverseSalesCapital.
terminal Consistency Proof
With constant final growth g and margin m, explicit reinvestment = (R_t - R_t-1) * (1+g)*m*(1-tax)/ROIC = NOPAT_t*g/ROIC. Thus final FCFF*(1+g) equals terminal-year NOPAT*(1-g/ROIC). The (1+g) factor matches the existing engine contemporaneous delta-sales convention to its terminal g/ROIC convention.
discounting
Use sampled WACC each year and same terminal WACC; taxes fixed unless user changes the scalar tax rate.
controls
Keep scalar assumptions editable, derive overrides inside the shared current valuation path. Do not persist generated arrays as user-authored overrides. Every Monte Carlo draw must run the same adapter.
zero Margin Boundary
When targetMargin=0, terminal intensity is zero. If the existing engine requires a finite positive salesCapital override, use Number.MAX_VALUE as a documented numerical limiting representation instead of Infinity; its resulting investment is negligible at monetary precision. Deterministic and simulation must share the same convention.

rationale
rationale · 6 records
  1. The issuer reported Q2 2026 revenue of $191.9m and guided Q3 to $255–290m. A front-loaded growth path with a fast decline from 60% to 40%, 30% and 20% is a bounded analyst illustration of ramp then slowdown, not a forecast derived directly from units or guidance.
  2. Management described approximate 200,000 monthly capacity and an expected 650,000 by year-end 2026. Capacity is not recognized revenue or guaranteed utilization; no direct multiplication of capacity by an invented selling price is used.
  3. The initial margin is reported GAAP TTM EBIT/revenue. Conditional break-even by year 2 and 12% mature margin by year 6 are analyst operating-leverage judgments; non-GAAP net income is not substituted for GAAP EBIT.
  4. Initial 0.8x sales/capital remains a conservative capital-heavy input; the temporary twofold utilization improvement is assumed, motivated by already funded construction and equipment prepayments, not by a verified incremental asset-turnover ratio.
  5. Capital intensity subsequently converges to the independently specified mature marginal ROIC, allowing competitive erosion of the higher mid-ramp return and eliminating a mechanical terminal reinvestment jump.
  6. All forecast growth, margin, capital-efficiency and risk values remain editable or sampled. The fixed weights describe transition shape, not independent reported facts or probabilities.
default Output Interpretation
The shared staged default still has negative operating enterprise value and common residual; show both raw residual and limited-liability floor, plus funding needs. It does not price abandonment, future funding access, default, recovery or an option to change strategy.
